svg.title: Four Python number types compared: int, float, Decimal, and Fraction, with the trade-off each makes
svg.text: Whole numbers, exact and unlimited: Python grows them as large as memory allows (no overflow).
Use for: counting, indexing, whole cents, anything discrete. Example: 2 ** 100 is exact.
64-bit IEEE 754. Fast and huge range, but ~15-17 significant digits and rounding error in base 2.
Use for: measurements, science, graphics, model weights. Not for exact money. 0.1+0.2 != 0.3.
Exact base-10 arithmetic with a chosen number of places. Slower, but no surprise rounding.
Use for: money, tax, invoices, anything audited. Build from strings: Decimal("0.1"), not Decimal(0.1).
Exact ratio of two ints (numerator / denominator). Perfect for rational math; slowest of the four.
Use for: exact ratios and probabilities. Example: Fraction(1, 3) * 3 == 1 exactly.
Rule of thumb: exact + whole -> int; exact + decimal money -> Decimal; exact ratio -> Fraction; everything else -> float.
